description: Le présent avis vise à mettre en place un système de qualification des entreprises pour le renouvellement du contrôle de vitesse (ci-après “KV”) de la Ligne A du RER exploitée par la RATP afin de s’assurer que la compétence, l’organisation et le savoir-faire des entreprises vouées à intervenir sur son réseau garantissent un niveau suffisant de qualité des prestations et plus particulièrement au regard de la sécurité ferroviaire. Seules les entreprises ayant fait l’objet, au jour du lancement de la consultation, d’une décision de qualification intermédiaire sur la base du présent système de qualification et de son cahier des charges pourront être consultées pour le marché de Conception/Déploiement du SACEM-KCVB NG. Ce marché de déploiement du SACEM-KCVB NG sera alloti en plusieurs lots. Seules les entreprises ayant fait l’objet d’une décision de qualification finale sur la base du présent système de qualification et de son cahier des charges pourront être attributaires de lots du marché de Conception/Déploiement du SACEM-KCVB NG. --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- Long de 109 kilomètres, le réseau RER A est principalement exploité par la RATP, à l’exception des branches de Cergy et Poissy qui relèvent de la SNCF à l’ouest de Nanterre-Préfecture. Le domaine RATP de la ligne A du RER est équipé de 2 contrôles de vitesse : - SACEM (et PA SACEM) de Nanterre Préfecture jusqu’à Noisy Champs (Branche MLV) et Fontenay sous-bois (Branche Boissy St Leger), - KCVB sur le reste du domaine. Le domaine RFN est uniquement équipé de KCVB d’origine de marchés propres à la SNCF. Le SACEM et le KCVB ont été mis en service sur le domaine RATP respectivement en 1989 et en 1997. EIT Urban Mobility community is made of over 270 partners and larger ecosystem of more than 1,200 stakeholders as we work together to make the transition to more sustainable urban mobility and liveable urban spaces. This community includes industry, including large enterprises, SMEs, and startups, universities and education institutions; students and alumni; research and technology organisations; governments at local, regional, national and EU-level; and non-governmental organisations (NGOs). Two years ago, EIT Urban Mobility launched its private digital community platform, Mobility Innovators, which brings together our vibrant community of innovators described above. The platform already has more than 1,500 active users and serves as the central platform for collaboration and engagement within our community. Mobility Innovators enables partners and stakeholders to access information, documents and opportunities shared by EIT Urban Mobility, register for events, and engage in discussions with peers across sectors. It connects organisations from industry, research, academia, and the public sector, fostering collaboration to advance the transition towards more sustainable and liveable urban mobility. Our goal in this next phase is to further grow and activate the community, expand platform functionalities, and enhance user experience to ensure Mobility Innovators continues to support EIT Urban Mobility’s role as Europe’s leading innovation community for urban mobility.

description: Deze aankondiging is geen oproep aan bestaande gekwalificeerde aannemers om al hun documenten i.k.v. hun kwalificatiedossier opnieuw in te dienen. Dit betreft louter een herpublicatie van het bestaande kwalificatiedossier SYN20W008. Er wijzigt niets, met uitzondering dat – ondanks de vermelding in ons kwalificatiesysteem – Blaaswerken glasvezel niet meer tot de activiteiten van Synductis behoort. Reeds gekwalificeerde aannemers voor één of meerdere van de activiteiten verbonden aan dit kwalificatiedossier dienen niet op deze publicatie te reageren. Synductis heeft als aanbesteder een kwalificatiesysteem gecreëerd. Hiervoor is een lijst van documenten samengesteld die de kandidaat dient aan te reiken om een ontvankelijk kandidatuurdossier in te dienen. De kandidaat kan enkel gekwalificeerd worden voor activiteiten die hij ook daadwerkelijk zelf kan en zal uitvoeren. Het voorwerp van de erkenningsregeling “aanneming nutswerken” is het aanleggen van een lijst van erkende aannemers voor het uitvoeren van werken binnen volgende disciplines: • Graven van sleuven • Graven van putten • Plaatsen en afwerken van leidingen ondergronds • Gestuurde boringen • Blaaswerken glasvezel Dit kwalificatiesysteem zal gebruikt worden als oproep tot mededinging voor plaatsingsprocedures van concrete opdrachten of raamovereenkomsten door Synductis of één of meerdere van zijn vennoten, al dan niet in combinatie met andere kwalificatiesystemen. Er kan een selectie worden gemaakt op basis van een combinatie van de verschillende kwalificatielijsten. Bij externe links vindt u de link naar het kwalificatiedossier van Fluvius en het kwalificatiedossier van de drinkwatermaatschappijen Pidpa, Farys, De Watergroep en AGSO Knokke-Heist.

title: Ireland – Public road transport services – Qualification System for National Shared Micromobility Schemes
description: The National Transport Authority (the “Authority”) wishes to establish a Qualification System in relation to contracts to operate certain Shared Micromobility Schemes throughout Ireland. This Qualification System will enable the procurement (by way of call off competitions), of operator(s) to supply and operate Shared Micromobility Scheme(s) in urban areas. The term of the Qualification System shall be five (5) years and shall commence on 14th February 2025. A candidate may seek admission to this Qualification System at any time during its term. The Qualification System shall be established and maintained by the Authority. Other contracting authorities may utilise the Qualification System to facilitate call off competitions pertaining to the operation of Shared Micromobility Schemes or shared micromobility projects funded by the Authority. Each call off contract is expected to comprise of, but not limited to the following principal obligations: • Provide, operate and maintain shared micromobility vehicles, (which can include bikes, e-bikes, e-scooters and/or e-cargo bikes) for the duration of the respective call-off contract; • Provide, operate and maintain a secure e-commerce platform for the duration of the respective call-off contract; • Operate a reliable and safe shared micromobility service as set out in the call-off contract; and • Promote the use of shared micromobility to encourage user demand. Under each call off competition, the services to be provided by the operator shall be defined by a services specification provided within the relevant tender documents and draft contract, but may comprise of one (1) or more of the following modes: • shared bikes; • shared e-bikes; • shared e-scooters; and/or • shared e-cargo bikes. Individual contracts may include: • one (1) or more of the modes detailed above, depending on local needs; and/or • one (1) or more operators, depending on local needs. Individual contracts under this Qualification System will involve varied operating business models depending on the circumstances of the contract in question. Such operating business models may include but are not limited to the following: • Operating contract; • Public/Private partnership (with or without revenue support); and/or • Licence/service permits. A range of tariffs shall be required to maximise user demand for the schemes. Individual contracts may include the following: • Subscription based tariffs (for frequent users); and/or • Single trip/Pay as You Go tariffs (for less frequent users). Individual contracts may include both tariffs set by the Authority or contracting authority and/or the operator(s). The provision of shared micromobility services require partnership working between the public sector and private sector operators. This can include financial support to both launch and grow service provision. Individual contracts may include: • Capital funding to support the implementation or expansion of a scheme; and/or • Revenue funding to support the ongoing operations of a scheme. Where shared micromobility schemes are already in existence, there may be existing on-street infrastructure and vehicles. Individual contracts may include options such as the following: • To re-use existing infrastructure and vehicles where possible; and/or • To replace existing infrastructure and vehicles as required. Full details of the Qualification System (including its operation) are provided within the Pre-Qualification Documents, which are available to all interested economic operators. All interested economic operators are now invited to submit a Pre-Qualification Submission for admission onto the Qualification System as set out in the Pre-Qualification Documents.

title: Neighbourhood COPD Risk Stratification Project - PCN Collaboration
description:
PSR MSP Process for the provision of primary care respiratory services for the identification and treatment of COPD.

CPV code: 85121000-6 Medical Practice & Related Services

Advances in COPD treatment and management provide an opportunity to improve outcomes through earlier identification and intervention using a risk-based approach to care, focused on identifying patients at greatest risk and providing timely access to specialist support and treatment.

This project aims to develop and implement a specialist-led, integrated neighbourhood model of care for people living with COPD across Hull and East Yorkshire. Using digital risk stratification and multidisciplinary specialist review, the project will proactively identify high-risk patients, support preventative intervention, and improve access to specialist care within community settings, in line with NHS priorities to shift care from hospitals to communities and from treatment to prevention.

Primary Care Networks (PCNs) will be appointed to act as delivery partners in the implementation and evaluation of this model. Working alongside specialist respiratory teams, based at Hull University Teaching Hospital, participating PCNs will support the identification, review and management of high-risk patients, while helping to build capability within primary care. The project will test the feasibility and impact of this neighbourhood-based approach and generate learning to inform future commissioning decisions and potential wider adoption across the Humber region and beyond.

A suitable Provider shall be a Primary Care Network (PCN) or primary care organisation serving a registered population of at least 30,000 patients, demonstrating the scale, infrastructure, and capability required to deliver high-quality, sustainable respiratory services within populations where the recorded QOF COPD prevalence exceeds 2.5%, demonstrating experience in meeting the needs of communities with a significant burden of respiratory disease.

Please refer to the Services Specifications for full details.

description: NHS South West London Integrated Care Board (SWL ICB) is carrying out preliminary market engagement ahead of a potential procurement of a Population Health Management (PHM), Population Segmentation and Risk Stratification platform, expected to be conducted through the G-Cloud 15 framework (RM1557.15), Lot 2b Software as a Service. This Request for Information (RFI) asks suppliers to describe their current capability against the full draft SWL PHM Service Specification. NHS South West London Integrated Care Board (SWL ICB) is seeking supplier information and indicative commercial proposals ahead of a planned procurement for a Population Health Management (PHM), Population Segmentation, Risk Stratification and Impactability Modelling solution for its registered population of approximately 1.78 million residents across Croydon, Kingston, Merton, Richmond, Sutton and Wandsworth. The requirement is intended to support the development of Integrated Neighbourhood Teams, proactive care, health inequalities reduction and population-based commissioning. The proposed solution should provide a clinically validated capability to segment the population, identify individuals at greatest risk of poor outcomes, determine which patients are most likely to benefit from proactive intervention, and support care coordination and neighbourhood delivery through actionable intelligence integrated into clinical workflows. The solution must support interoperability with existing SWL systems, including GP clinical systems and SWL Health Insights, and align with NHS clinical safety, information governance and interoperability standards. Suppliers on the G-Cloud 15 framework are invited to submit information on their current capability and provide indicative pricing proposals covering: 1. The full end-to-end service, including Population Health Management, Population Segmentation, Risk Stratification, Impactability Modelling, cohort identification, analytics, dashboards, integration, implementation, training and ongoing support. 2. A standalone Risk Stratification and Impactability Modelling service, including clinically validated models for emergency admission risk, emergency department attendance risk, care coordination risk, frailty, end of life prediction and impactability modelling, together with the associated implementation, integration and support costs. This reflects SWL ICB's current business case focus on procuring a dedicated risk stratification and impactability capability while maintaining alignment with wider London population segmentation developments. Suppliers should clearly distinguish between costs for the full service and costs for the standalone Risk Stratification and Impactability Modelling component, including one-off implementation costs and annual recurring charges. title: PRJ 2305 - Intercultural Therapeutic Service for Lewisham
description: NHS South East London Integrated Care Board (SEL ICB) intends to award a single contract for the delivery of the Intercultural Therapeutic Service (ITS) in the London Borough of Lewisham. The Intercultural Therapeutic Service (ITS) provides specialist psychological support for Lewisham residents experiencing emotional distress, trauma, isolation and mental health difficulties where cultural, racial, migratory, faith, identity and social experiences are significant factors in presentation and recovery. The service was established to address recognise inequalities in access to and outcomes from mental health services amongst communities who may be underserved by conventional psychological support pathways, including people from Black African, Black Caribbean and other ethnically diverse communities, refugees and asylum seekers, migrants, and individuals with experiences of complex trauma. The service forms part of Lewisham's broader commitment to addressing mental health inequalities and improving culturally responsive support. It complements, rather than duplicates, existing statutory and NHS mental health provision. The Commissioner considers that delivery of the service requires a distinctive combination of intercultural psychotherapy, trauma-informed practice, racially aware therapeutic approaches, specialist supervision arrangements and workforce development functions that are not routinely available through standard counselling or wellbeing services. The Intercultural Therapeutic Service is not a standard counselling service. The model integrates: • intercultural psychotherapy; • racially-aware and anti-oppressive therapeutic practice; • trauma-informed approaches; • culturally adapted therapeutic interventions; • multilingual provision where appropriate; • reflective and relational therapeutic approaches; • academic and clinical expertise through a specialist training environment. A key distinguishing feature of the service is the integration of therapeutic delivery within a specialist academic-clinical model. Therapeutic practitioners are supported through a structured supervision framework involving qualified psychotherapists, experienced clinical supervisors and academic expertise. This enables intensive reflective practice, robust clinical governance and continuous service development. The Commissioner considers this supervision structure to be a distinctive component of the model, combining specialist clinical supervision, academic expertise, reflective practice and workforce development within a single service. The combination of intercultural psychotherapy, racially-aware practice and enhanced clinical supervision is not routinely available through existing mental health pathways and provides a level of specialism that would be difficult to replicate through a generic counselling or wellbeing service. The service therefore represents a specialised offer which contributes innovation within the local mental health system whilst maintaining appropriate standards of clinical governance and quality assurance. Independent evaluation of the service has demonstrated positive service-user outcomes, successful engagement of populations experiencing mental health inequalities, and evidence that the model is reaching individuals whose needs may not be fully met through conventional psychological support pathways. The Commissioner intends that the next phase of the service will build upon this evidence and further evaluate integration, accessibility and scalability. A key objective of the service is to improve access to psychological support for residents who are historically less likely to engage with, benefit from, or remain within traditional mental health services. The contract value is £150,000 for a period of 18-months. The process being followed is a Most Suitable Provider Process under the Provider Selection Regime 2023.

title: South London Outreach Services
description: NHS South East London & NHS South West London Integrated Care Boards are seeking to commission an integrated Immunisation Outreach, Hospital In-Reach and Vaccination Engagement Services across South London for 1 April 2027 to 31 March 2028 with option to extend for a further 12 months to 31 March 2029. The service forms a key part of the South London Vaccination and Immunisation Programme and will support the ambition to protect the health and wellbeing of residents through increasing equitable access to vaccination and preventative healthcare interventions, reducing health inequalities and improving population health outcomes. The service will ensure that all eligible individuals, regardless of age, ethnicity, race, disability, socioeconomic status, pregnancy status, protected characteristic or geographical location, have access to timely, convenient and accessible vaccination opportunities delivered through a range of community and healthcare settings. The Provider will deliver an integrated model of community outreach, hospital in-reach, vaccination engagement and proactive population outreach across the London Boroughs of Bexley, Bromley, Greenwich, Lambeth, Lewisham and Southwark for SE London and Croydon, Kingston, Merton, Richmond, Sutton & Wandsworth for SW London. Delivery will be tailored to local population need and informed by population health intelligence, vaccination uptake data and identified health inequalities. Services will be delivered through a range of accessible venues, locations, days and times, including community venues, faith and cultural settings, mobile and pop-up clinics, hospitals, inpatient wards, outpatient departments and other settings where eligible individuals can be offered vaccination opportunistically. A key objective of the service is to generate and maintain public trust and confidence through sustained community engagement, culturally competent approaches and partnership working with trusted local organisations and community leaders. The Provider will actively address vaccine hesitancy and misinformation, promote choice and improve confidence in communities known to experience lower uptake. The service will place particular emphasis on identifying, prioritising and reaching vulnerable, underserved and under-vaccinated populations, including Core20PLUS5 populations immunosuppressed individuals, people with complex long-term conditions, ethnically diverse communities, socially excluded groups, pregnant women and other cohorts identified through national and local vaccination priorities. The Provider will establish and operate a dedicated vaccination contact centre to proactively engage patients; support appointment booking and undertake targeted outbound engagement with clinically vulnerable and high-risk groups. This will include proactive outreach to immunosuppressed and severely immunocompromised individuals who may require additional support to access vaccination services. The Provider will work collaboratively as a system partner with NHS Trusts, Primary Care Networks, General Practice, Community Pharmacy, Local Authorities, Public Health teams and Voluntary, Community, Faith and Social Enterprise organisations to ensure services are accessible, coordinated and responsive to local need. Through community outreach, hospital in-reach and targeted engagement activity, the service will seek to increase vaccination uptake across South London, reduce the incidence and impact of COVID-19 and other vaccine-preventable diseases, minimise avoidable illness, hospital admissions and deaths, and ensure that individuals and communities are protected quickly and effectively. The provider is expected to demonstrate a proven track record in delivering community outreach, hospital in-reach and vaccination contact centre services for a minimum of three years in South London, with prior experience in meeting the key objectives and service requirements as outlined. Annual contract value: £840,000.

title: COBR Strategic Partnership (Private Sector Resilience Project)
description: The purpose of this Prior Information Notice (PIN) is to notify all interested parties of the Cabinet Office's intention to undertake a commercial procurement exercise. The exercise aims to appoint a world-class Strategic Partner to provide a managed service. The Cabinet Office Briefing Rooms (COBR) Directorate requires a world-class strategic partner to co-design and co-deliver high-impact, targeted resilience workshops, scenario exercises, and potential follow-on consultancy to UK and international private sector clients. The primary objective is to operationalise resilience within the private sector by translating central government crisis doctrine and leadership expertise into actionable strategies for C-suite executives and operational leads, aligned with existing industry practice. COBR serves as the central hub for the UK Government's whole-of-government crisis response mechanism. National resilience is a whole-of-society endeavour. This partnership seeks to support business and organisational resilience by establishing a scalable framework for clients to adopt UK-standard crisis doctrine while creating a formal feedback loop where private sector insights directly inform future national resilience policies. This agreement is a zero-cost contract to the public buyer. The Cabinet Office will not pay the partner. The successful supplier will bear all delivery and travel expenses, motivated by the commercial branding rights, reputational gains, and high-level insights gained from working alongside COBR. The partnership will operate on a 'Value for Money' basis for the taxpayer, using a revenue-sharing or licence fee model where the partner pays an agreed annual fee and/or percentage of gross workshop revenue to the Crown for the commercial use of COBR-branded materials and doctrine.

title: Neighbourhood COPD Risk Stratification Population Health Project
description:
PSR MSP Process for the provision of primary care respiratory services for the identification and treatment of COPD.

CPV code: 85121000-6 Medical Practice & Related Services

This project aims to develop and implement a specialist-led, integrated neighbourhood model of care for people living with COPD across Hull and East Yorkshire. Part of the project will involve developing a risk stratification tool, utilising linked system level data held by Humber and North Yorkshire Integrated Care Board (ICB), Appendix 1 sets out the proposed data flow to support COPD Population Level Health Management.

By developing, testing and implementing a population health, digital risk stratification tool, the project will proactively identify high-risk patients, support preventative intervention, and improve access to specialist care within community settings, in line with NHS priorities to shift care from hospitals to communities and from treatment to prevention.

Primary Care Networks (PCNs) will be invited to participate as delivery partners in the implementation, ongoing development, and evaluation of the proposed model. Working collaboratively with specialist respiratory services provided by Hull University Teaching Hospitals NHS Trust, participating PCNs will support the identification, review, and proactive management of high-risk patients, whilst contributing to the development of respiratory capability and capacity within primary care.

The project will test the feasibility and impact of this neighbourhood-based approach and generate learning to inform future commissioning decisions and potential wider adoption across the Humber region and beyond.

A suitable Provider shall be a Primary Care Network (PCN) or primary care organisation serving a registered population of at least 20,000 patients, demonstrating the scale, infrastructure, and capability required to deliver high-quality, sustainable respiratory services within populations where the recorded QOF COPD prevalence exceeds 2.0%, demonstrating experience in meeting the needs of communities with a significant burden of respiratory disease.

Ideally 2 PCNs will be awarded contracts.

Please note that organisations already participating in, or progressing towards contract for, another COPD integrated risk stratification project involving partnership working between specialist respiratory services and primary care will not be eligible to participate in both projects concurrently.

In the event that more than two compliant Expressions of Interest are received, providers will be selected based on COPD prevalence, with priority given to those serving populations with the highest prevalence.

Please refer to the full Services Specifications document for further details.
